title: Mechanism-defined diseases in place of the major syndromes

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a clinically usable way to divide at least one major psychiatric syndrome—such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or major depression—into distinct diseases defined by causal mechanisms that can be identified in individual people. Instead of assigning only a label based on a pattern of symptoms, clinicians could establish which disease process is responsible. The intended scope is most patients within at least one major syndrome; it does not require a universal diagnostic test for every psychiatric disorder.

Conceptual distinction: a biological association or a useful predictor is not, by itself, a mechanism-defined disease. A genetic score, inflammatory marker or imaging pattern might distinguish groups or predict an outcome without establishing the causal process operating in a particular patient. This concept requires both an individually applicable classification and independent evidence that the mechanisms defining its classes have the claimed causal role. Simply giving existing syndromes biological names would not meet that ambition.

The documented starting point is a diagnostic system that supplies a common symptom-based language. The ECNP-coordinated precision-psychiatry roadmap proposes incorporating biological evidence into that framework and testing its value for patient stratification and treatment. This supports the direction of the proposed innovation, while leaving open the stronger achievement of identifying distinct causal diseases within a syndrome.

significance.text: Conditional impact assessment: a successful partition would supply a new disease map and a scientific basis for changing psychiatry’s primary diagnostic language. People who currently share a syndrome label could receive different diagnoses because their illnesses arise through different mechanisms. Clinical adoption would still require usable tests, implementation and evidence that the resulting decisions improve care; discovery of the classification would not itself accomplish those steps.

If the classes independently predict illness course and differences in treatment benefit, the classification could support more informative prognosis and treatment selection. These are separate clinical achievements that must be demonstrated, rather than assumed from biological plausibility. The roadmap’s emphasis on predictive validation for stratification and treatment is consistent with that distinction, although its retained abstract and figure-caption text do not demonstrate the proposed disease map.

Impact analogy: pathogen identification reorganizing infectious disease illustrates the possible scale of a shift from symptom patterns to causal diagnoses. It is an analogy, not an established equivalence or a prediction that psychiatric diseases will have similarly discrete causes. Even a successful mechanism-based classification would not guarantee an effective treatment for every class. Developing medicines from confirmed human mechanisms remains a further innovation, represented here by PSY-05.

Conditional downstream possibilities include more coherent research cohorts and trials that test an intervention in patients whose disease mechanism it is intended to affect. These benefits would depend on the classification being sufficiently reproducible, clinically relevant and practical. Separating one rare mechanistic condition from a much larger unresolved syndrome could be valuable for those patients, but would not by itself deliver the broad reorganization proposed here.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a clinically validated disease partition that holds in individuals. Evidence of differences between groups does not establish that a test can identify an individual’s causal disease. The supplied commentary argues for convergence among diagnostic validators and criticizes the validity of existing categories. That is a useful statement of the scientific problem, but it is the authors’ assessment rather than proof that every proposed classifier has failed or that one particular explanation accounts for all diagnostic limitations.

Scientific synthesis: causal heterogeneity within current labels is a motivating hypothesis, not an established sole barrier in the supplied evidence. The difficult task is to connect a measurable feature in a patient to a causal mechanism, show that the proposed classes have defensible boundaries, and obtain independent validators that support those same distinctions. A classifier that predicts outcomes could remain useful without satisfying the stronger claim that its classes are diseases defined by necessary mechanisms.

Engineering synthesis: the classification would need reproducible individual assignments and measurements that work in ordinary clinical populations, rather than only in a selected research sample. It would also need to separate differences in baseline prognosis from differences in benefit caused by a particular treatment. The supplied evidence does not establish whether inflammation-based or imaging-based approaches have solved these problems, and limitations of the particular polygenic scores reviewed cannot settle those wider questions.

current_state.text: A July 20, 2026 commentary by S. Nassir Ghaemi and Mark L. Ruffalo describes planned changes associated with the Future DSM Strategic Committee and argues that diagnostic validity remains inadequately addressed. The supplied review examined the complete commentary, but the committee’s primary strategy document was not supplied. The criticism therefore belongs to the commentary’s authors and should not be presented as a demonstrated field-wide consensus or as a comprehensive account of DSM development.

The ECNP-coordinated precision-psychiatry roadmap, published June 19, 2025, proposes an iterative framework that incorporates biological evidence into symptom-based syndromes and evaluates its predictive value for stratification and treatment. It documents a research program rather than completion of an individual mechanism-defined disease map. The supplied review used the PubMed abstract and retained figure-caption text; the full paper and the figure graphic were not inspected.

A 2025 UK Biobank analysis by Mollon and colleagues studied 408,853 White British participants. Among people in the top 5 percent of one schizophrenia polygenic risk score, only 47.7 percent were also in the top 5 percent of another schizophrenia score. Reported specificity across all tested scores was 50.7–56.4 percent; that range included a type 2 diabetes score as well as psychiatric scores. These findings show limited stability and specificity for the scores and population studied. They do not establish that every possible polygenic score is incapable of useful individual prediction, nor do they establish a causal disease partition. The numerical findings are reported in the retained abstract; the full paper was not reviewed.

A December 10, 2025 Nature news report by Max Kozlov describes psychiatric conditions as falling into five broad genetic clusters. The retained standfirst and opening paragraph support that limited account of shared genetic structure. The article body stopped at access options, and the underlying Grotzinger and colleagues primary paper was not inspected. This material therefore does not establish that clinicians can assign an individual to a mechanism-defined disease. The access limitation also does not show that the underlying genetic result is false.

Anti-NMDA-receptor encephalitis supplies an example of an autoimmune mechanism that can present with psychiatric symptoms, including psychosis. Separately, Pollak and colleagues’ meta-analysis, published in the September 2014 issue of Psychological Medicine, reported serum IgG anti-NMDA-receptor antibodies in 21 of 1,441 patients, or 1.46 percent, drawn from schizophrenia, schizophrenia-spectrum disorder and first-episode psychosis samples without clinical signs of encephalitis. The assays were heterogeneous. The authors left unresolved whether antibody-positive patients had distinct pathology or treatment response, so this prevalence cannot be treated as the fraction already assigned to a validated causal disease subtype.

For the antibody meta-analysis, the supplied review examined the abstract rather than the full paper. The record lists an erratum whose text was not supplied, and newer population fractions were not re-estimated. These limitations preserve uncertainty about interpretation and subsequent developments without negating the abstract’s reported finding.

Evidence boundary: the supplied dated material does not demonstrate completion of PSY-01, but it also does not establish comprehensive field status as of November 1, 2026. No bounded freshness search record was supplied. The appropriate conclusion is that these sources document research directions, specific predictive limitations and a mechanistic example—not that every relevant approach across psychiatry has been assessed.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: use a preregistered, prospectively followed cohort representing ordinary clinical practice. Assign most people who would currently receive one selected major syndromic label to mechanism-defined classes before their outcomes are known. Define coverage, assignment rules, uncertain cases and clinically important performance in advance. Separating a rare mimic while leaving the great majority mechanistically unclassified would not satisfy this proposed scope.
completion_criteria.label: Most patients receive mechanism-defined assignments prospectively before outcomes are known

completion_criteria.text: Proposed causal requirement: obtain independent mechanistic evidence establishing the claimed causal role of the defining mechanisms. Predictive accuracy, clustering or differential outcomes alone would not prove diseases defined by necessary mechanisms. The eventual protocol would need to specify what evidence can justify that stronger causal claim rather than substituting an associated biomarker for the mechanism itself.
completion_criteria.label: Independent mechanistic evidence establishes causal roles of defining mechanisms

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical validation: class membership measured before outcome should predict course and differential treatment response in at least two classes. The treatment comparison should use a design capable of distinguishing a treatment-effect difference from a general prognostic difference—for example, an appropriately designed randomized comparison. Once class membership is known, the old syndromic label should add no clinically important predictive information within the tested scope. A definition of clinical importance would need to be specified before evaluation.
completion_criteria.label: Classes predict course and differential treatment response beyond syndromic labels

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundary: replicate the classification and its clinical value in a second health system, examining reproducibility of measurements and individual assignments as well as outcome prediction. Document the populations, care settings, unassigned patients and uncertain cases to which the demonstration applies. Finite cohorts establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Classification and clinical value replicate in a second health system

completion_criteria.text: These criteria are proposals for a convincing demonstration, not an established consensus standard. No numerical accuracy threshold is adopted, including any figure above 90 percent. The meanings of most patients and clinically important prediction remain protocol decisions requiring justification. Completion would not require effective medicines for every class, a universal psychiatric test or immediate replacement of diagnostic manuals throughout clinical practice.
completion_criteria.label: Protocol definitions for patient coverage and clinical importance are justified

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison with PSY-05, Medicines designed from a confirmed human disease mechanism: PSY-01 concerns identifying and classifying causal diseases; PSY-05 concerns creating medicines from confirmed mechanisms. A validated disease map could supply targets and define eligible patient groups, but classification does not itself produce an effective medicine. Conversely, a mechanism-based medicine for one condition would not necessarily partition most patients within a major syndrome.

Roster-based comparison with PSY-06, A clinical instrument that reads an individual’s psychiatric state: PSY-01 asks which mechanism-defined disease a person has, while PSY-06 concerns measuring the person’s psychiatric state, potentially repeatedly over time. A state measurement could help validate or monitor disease classes, but changing state and disease identity are distinct questions. This boundary follows the supplied descriptions; a full PSY-06 specification was not provided.

Roster-based comparison with PSY-02, A treatment that changes the course of schizophrenia, and PSY-03, Ending the relapsing course of severe mood disorders: these concern treatment outcomes rather than a new diagnostic partition. Mechanism-defined classes might reveal which patients benefit from such treatments. A treatment could nevertheless change course or prevent relapse without reorganizing the syndrome into causal diseases, and a new classification could be valid before those treatment outcomes become achievable.

Roster-based comparison with PSY-04, Primary prevention that lowers incidence of a major disorder, and PSY-11, Prevention of post-traumatic stress disorder by blocking consolidation: these concern preventing illness. Discovering causal disease mechanisms could inform prevention, but PSY-01 requires neither a demonstrated reduction in incidence nor an intervention on memory consolidation. Successful prevention would likewise not automatically establish a broad mechanism-based classification.

Roster-based comparison with PSY-07, Reliable causal control of a core symptom by a defined circuit: causal control of a symptom could contribute mechanistic evidence, but it need not identify the disease causing that symptom. A symptom-relevant circuit might be shared across several diseases. PSY-01 therefore requires more than demonstrating that manipulating a circuit changes one feature of a syndrome.

Roster-based comparison with PSY-08, Selective and durable modification of a pathological memory; PSY-09, A time-limited reset of severe addiction; PSY-10, Reopening plasticity that can repair an established psychiatric deficit; and PSY-12, A session-level amplifier that lets brief psychotherapy match a full course: these describe intervention capabilities rather than a disease taxonomy. Each could benefit from better patient classification, or provide evidence relevant to mechanisms, without independently delivering the broad diagnostic partition proposed by PSY-01. These distinctions are conceptual comparisons from the supplied titles; the other entries’ full criteria were not supplied.

change_log.change: Preserved PSY-01’s identity and broad within-syndrome scope while explicitly distinguishing causal diseases from predictive classes and biological relabeling.
change_log.reason: The concept requires individual identification of causal disease mechanisms, which associations or predictive stratification alone do not establish.

change_log.change: Qualified causal heterogeneity as a motivating hypothesis and separated scientific validation barriers from practical measurement and implementation requirements.
change_log.reason: The supplied sources do not establish causal heterogeneity as the sole barrier or exhaustively assess genetic, inflammatory and imaging classifiers.

change_log.change: Separated the new disease map, validated prognosis, treatment selection, clinical adoption and development of effective medicines.
change_log.reason: These are distinct achievements; none follows automatically from naming a mechanism. The infectious-disease comparison remains a conditional impact analogy.

change_log.change: Added independent causal validation and a treatment-comparison design that distinguishes treatment-effect differences from prognostic differences.
change_log.reason: The original prospective prediction criteria did not by themselves establish necessary mechanisms or differential treatment benefit.

change_log.change: Retained the proposed prospective cohort, broad coverage and second-health-system replication criteria while clarifying their provisional nature and finite scope.
change_log.reason: These are coherent proposed demonstrations, not published standards or evidence of universality. No numerical accuracy threshold was supplied.

change_log.change: Corrected the DSM commentary attribution to S. Nassir Ghaemi and Mark L. Ruffalo and identified its criticism as their assessment.
change_log.reason: The review verified both authors and distinguished the commentary from the unsupplied primary committee strategy document.

change_log.change: Restored the polygenic-score study’s population, sample size, 47.7 percent risk-group overlap and exact specificity range, including the range’s coverage of a diabetes score.
change_log.reason: The earlier account omitted useful quantitative detail and overgeneralized the results to all psychiatric polygenic scores and individual identification.

change_log.change: Preserved the five-cluster genetic news finding while documenting partial access and the absence of primary-paper review.
change_log.reason: The retained excerpt supports shared genetic structure, but does not establish individual diagnostic capability; missing access is not evidence against the reported result.

change_log.change: Replaced the claim that antibody positivity demonstrates a real mechanistic disease split with the reported prevalence and unresolved interpretation.
change_log.reason: The meta-analysis included first-episode psychosis and explicitly left distinct pathology and treatment response unsettled. Antibody positivity alone does not diagnose a causal subtype.

change_log.change: Preserved abstract-only review, the uninspected figure graphic, the unsupplied erratum and the absence of a freshness search.
change_log.reason: Saved source records do not imply full scientific-document inspection or comprehensive field coverage through November 2026.

change_log.change: Expanded related-concept comparisons to cover every other supplied roster entry without merging them.
change_log.reason: The roster enables useful conceptual distinctions, while full specifications remain unavailable for verifying exact overlap.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish comprehensive field status as of November 1, 2026; no bounded freshness search record was provided.
The causal architecture within the selected major syndrome, the appropriate class boundaries and the evidence sufficient to establish necessary mechanisms remain unresolved.

An eventual protocol must operationalize most patients, clinically important incremental prediction, acceptable uncertainty and practical reproducibility; no numerical accuracy threshold has been set.

The polygenic-score results apply to the tested scores in White British UK Biobank participants. Performance of other scores, other populations and inflammation- or imaging-based classifiers was not comprehensively assessed.
The primary genetic study underlying the December 2025 Nature report was not inspected, and the full news article was inaccessible in the retained material.

The clinical meaning of serum IgG anti-NMDA-receptor antibody positivity in the reviewed primary-psychosis samples remains unresolved. The listed erratum was not supplied, and contemporary prevalence was not re-estimated.
Full texts and completion criteria for PSY-02 through PSY-12 were not supplied, so exact boundaries and duplication cannot be verified beyond the roster-based comparisons.
No substantive review correction was rejected; proposed examples of validation design remain explicitly proposals rather than evidence of an achieved innovation.

brief.title: Mental health diagnoses based on what causes illness
possible: People given the same diagnosis, such as major depression, could learn which disease process causes their illness. Clinicians could distinguish different diseases behind similar symptoms. This would work for most patients within at least one major psychiatric diagnosis.
why: A diagnosis based on causes could give patients a clearer picture of how their illness may develop and which treatment may help them. Researchers could test treatments in people who share the disease process those treatments target.

sources.who: S. Nassir Ghaemi and Mark L. Ruffalo
sources.showed: Their commentary argues that psychiatric diagnoses need agreement among symptoms, genetics, illness course and biological measurements to establish that they describe distinct diseases.
sources.cited_for: They explain why consistently assigning a diagnosis does not establish that it identifies a real disease.
sources.not_established: Their argument does not demonstrate a classification based on causes.

sources.who: Martien J. H. Kas and colleagues
sources.showed: They proposed a research framework for adding biological information to diagnoses based on symptoms and testing its value for treatment decisions.
sources.cited_for: Their roadmap describes a path toward diagnoses informed by biology.
sources.not_established: They did not demonstrate distinct causal diseases that clinicians can identify in individual patients.

sources.showed: They compared genetic risk scores, which combine many genetic variants into a risk estimate. The tested scores often disagreed about who had high risk among White British UK Biobank participants.
sources.quote: less than half of individuals identified as high risk with one PRS were identified as high risk with another PRS.
sources.cited_for: Their results expose limits of the tested genetic risk scores for individual decisions.
sources.not_established: The results neither rule out other scores nor identify causal diseases.

sources.showed: Their genetic analysis grouped psychiatric conditions into five broad clusters linked to particular genetic variants.
sources.quote: mental-health disorders fall into five clusters, each of them linked to a specific set of genetic variants.
sources.cited_for: The analysis supports shared genetic patterns across existing diagnoses.
sources.not_established: Shared genetic patterns do not establish which disease process causes an individual person's illness.

sources.showed: Their review found IgG antibodies, a type of immune protein, in 1.46% of patients with schizophrenia or related illnesses. These targeted NMDA receptors, which receive signals in cells.
sources.quote: Prevalence rates were greater in cases than controls only for IgG antibodies; other subclasses are of less certain aetiological relevance.
sources.cited_for: The review identifies a possible immune link in a minority of patients.
sources.not_established: Antibody positivity did not establish a distinct causal disease or a different response to treatment.

shown: An immune attack can cause brain inflammation with psychiatric symptoms. Pollak and colleagues also found antibodies in patients without clinical signs of that inflammation. This provides a possible lead toward separating diseases within existing diagnoses.
missing: A usable classification would need to identify the causal disease in most patients sharing a major psychiatric diagnosis.
Independent findings would need to establish that the defining processes cause illness, beyond merely predicting it.
The classes would need to improve predictions of illness course and treatment benefit, with results reproduced in another health system.

milestones.label: Most patients receive a diagnosis based on causes
milestones.explanation: A study representing ordinary care would assign most patients within a chosen diagnosis before outcomes are known, using rules set beforehand. This would establish broad coverage beyond rare exceptions.

milestones.label: Independent findings establish the causes
milestones.explanation: Independent studies would establish that each defining biological process has the claimed causal role. This would distinguish diseases from groups that merely share a measurable feature.

milestones.label: Classes predict illness course and treatment benefit
milestones.explanation: At least two classes would predict illness course and differences in treatment benefit, with no clinically important information added by the old diagnosis. This would establish their value for clinical decisions.

milestones.label: Results hold in another health system
milestones.explanation: A second health system would reproduce individual assignments and their clinical value, documenting uncertain and unassigned cases. This would establish how broadly the classification works.

milestones.label: Coverage and clinical value have justified definitions
milestones.explanation: The study rules would justify what counts as covering most patients and making clinically important predictions. This would make success assessable without requiring a treatment for every class.

uncertain: It remains unclear where disease boundaries lie within a major diagnosis and what evidence would establish the necessary causal processes.
The proposed milestones are not an agreed standard, and no numerical accuracy threshold has been set.
It remains unclear whether antibody-positive patients without brain inflammation have a distinct illness or benefit from different treatment.

page.title: Mechanism-based classification of psychiatric disorders
page.definition: Most patients within at least one major psychiatric syndrome, a diagnosis defined by symptoms, can be assigned individually to distinct diseases defined by causal mechanisms. Independent evidence establishes those mechanisms’ causal roles and the clinical relevance of the assignments.

goal.need: Individual diagnosis requires more than a biological association. A study published on 18 March 2025 compared polygenic risk scores, estimates combining many genetic variants, in 408,853 White British UK Biobank participants. Alternative scores often selected different people for the highest-risk group. The overlap below concerns inherited-risk estimates; it does not establish causal disease classes.

figures.caption: Agreement between alternative genetic risk scores for the same disorder
figures.note: Each highest-risk group comprised the top 5% of a score; the depression range covers comparisons among three scores.

statements.body: European College of Neuropsychopharmacology: Precision Psychiatry Roadmap steering committee
statements.quote: accurate stratification of heterogenous populations to biologically homogenous subpopulations
statements.context: The roadmap identifies this as a consequence of complementing symptom-based diagnoses with quantitative biological and behavioral measurements.

statements.quote: The authors propose a structured, dynamic process to integrate emerging knowledge about biological factors into the DSM, ultimately providing biologically grounded diagnostic categories.
statements.context: The announcement concerns the Future DSM Strategic Committee and its Biomarkers and Biological Factors Subcommittee.

completion.title: Most patients within one psychiatric syndrome receive independently validated causal disease assignments.
completion.criterion: In a prospectively assessed clinical cohort with one major psychiatric syndrome, an individually applicable classification assigns more than half of patients to at least two diseases distinguished by independently supported causal mechanisms. Independent studies validate the assignments and their clinical relevance. Predictive biomarkers alone do not establish causal disease identity. The majority-coverage boundary is Atlas-defined; the cited bodies have not adopted this completion test.
completion.set_by: The Atlas; fallback for the broad causal-classification capability, rather than an externally adopted disease-discovery standard.
completion.basis: Searched the ECNP roadmap, APA Future DSM material and neuroimaging consensus, and ACNP biomarker roadmap for a test of a causal partition covering most patients. Found biomarker-validation criteria, but no such completion test or agreed causal-evidence standard. The fallback preserves individual assignment, causal evidence and broad coverage; more than half operationalizes most.

milestones.title: Manipulating a candidate psychiatric disease mechanism changes the corresponding behavior in an animal model.
milestones.criterion: Experimental manipulation tests whether a human biological association causes the corresponding behavior in an animal model. The roadmap presents this as causal backtranslation, without a numerical effect threshold. A study in Brain’s January 2015 issue infused patient or control cerebrospinal fluid into mice; the behavioral experiments included 18 patient-fluid and 20 control-fluid mice. Anti-NMDA-receptor encephalitis fluid produced reversible memory deficits. This supports a specific autoimmune mechanism, not a partition of primary psychiatric syndromes.
milestones.set_by: ECNP-coordinated Precision Psychiatry Roadmap, translational predictive model systems section; an experimental approach, not a universal proof of human disease causation.
milestones.threshold_quote: activating the corresponding brain area and testing for effects on the specific behavior

milestones.title: A psychiatric diagnostic biomarker exceeds 80% sensitivity and 80% specificity.
milestones.criterion: Sensitivity exceeds 80% for detecting the reference disorder; specificity exceeds 80% against other psychiatric or medical disorders. The report conditions this template on accepting the reference diagnosis. It does not establish causal disease identity. On 14 August 2025, B-SNIP reported three biomarker-defined psychosis groups in 1,907 patients, 705 relatives and 895 healthy participants. That clustering result does not itself demonstrate this diagnostic test against independently established causal diseases.
milestones.set_by: APA Work Group on Neuroimaging Markers of Psychiatric Disorders, July 2012 report, page 5; conditional narrative criterion adapted from an Alzheimer’s disease template.
milestones.threshold_quote: have a sensitivity >80% for detecting a particular psychiatric disorder and a specificity of >80%

milestones.title: At least two independent investigator groups confirm a psychiatric diagnostic biomarker’s validity.
milestones.criterion: Two independent qualified investigator groups confirm diagnostic validity in peer-reviewed studies. Pollak and colleagues’ September 2014 meta-analysis found serum IgG anti-NMDA-receptor antibodies in 21 of 1,441 patients across seven psychosis studies without clinical signs of encephalitis. Assays were heterogeneous; distinct pathology and treatment response remained unresolved. Repeated antibody detection therefore did not establish a validated causal disease subtype.
milestones.set_by: APA Work Group on Neuroimaging Markers of Psychiatric Disorders, July 2012 report, page 5; proposed diagnostic-biomarker confirmation criterion.
milestones.threshold_quote: at least two independent sets of qualified investigators

milestones.title: Biomarker-guided psychiatric decisions yield reproducible clinical and functional improvement.
milestones.criterion: Clinical decisions enabled by a biomarker are reproducible and demonstrate measurable clinical and functional improvement; ACNP specifies no universal effect-size cutoff. A January 2013 report randomized 60 patients with treatment-resistant depression to infliximab or placebo, 30 per arm, for 12 weeks. There was no overall benefit on the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale. In the exploratory subgroup with baseline C-reactive protein above 5 mg/L, response (at least 50% score reduction at any visit) was 8/13 versus 3/9 (P=0.19). This did not validate a biomarker-guided care strategy.
milestones.set_by: American College of Neuropsychopharmacology Precompetitive Stakeholder Task Force, 18 September 2026 position paper, de-risking strategies section.
milestones.threshold_quote: its ability to demonstrate measurable clinical and functional improvement

not_found: No externally adopted completion test specifying patient coverage and sufficient causal evidence for this disease classification was found.
The APA’s 2026 biomarker-subcommittee article could not be opened; its public announcement was accessible.

results.finding: In 408,853 UK Biobank participants, schizophrenia polygenic risk scores had 90.2%–93.3% sensitivity.
results.detail: Specificity across all scores was 50.7%–56.4%, below the required threshold. The text does not specify the comparison groups underlying the abstract’s specificity estimate.
results.quote: PRS sensitivity was moderate for MDD (66.1%-74.4%) and AUD (72.3%-74.2%), moderate/good for T2D (77.3%-96.3%), and good for SCZ (90.2%-93.3%). Specificity was low for all PRSs (50.7%-56.4%).

results.finding: Across seven studies, 21 of 1,441 patients with psychosis had IgG anti-NMDA receptor antibodies.
results.detail: Antibody assays and patient characteristics were heterogeneous. The review did not establish distinct underlying pathology or treatment response, so repeated detection did not validate a diagnostic subtype.
results.quote: Seven studies were included, comprising 1441 patients, of whom 115 [7.98%, 95% confidence interval (CI) 6.69-9.50] were anti-NMDA receptor antibody positive. Of these, 21 (1.46%, 95% CI 0.94-2.23) patients were positive for antibodies of the IgG subclass.

results.finding: In mice given schizophrenia patient IgG, Y-maze performance decreased; 9 mice per group, p < 0.01.
results.detail: Removing anti-NCAM1 antibodies from patient IgG reversed the behavioral change. The study did not establish whether the antibodies cause symptoms in patients.
results.quote: Removal of anti-NCAM1 antibodies from purified IgG reversed the decrease in the alteration ratios. ∗∗p < 0.01 (n = 9 mice per group; Tukey’s HSD test).

results.finding: Human C4A-overexpressing mice showed altered anxiety-like behavior; 7 overexpressing and 8 comparison mice, P = 0.0140.
results.detail: Higher C4A expression is associated with schizophrenia risk in humans. In mice, overexpression changed center-zone rearing in an open-field test. The study does not establish that synapse loss caused the behavioral change.
results.quote:
However, overexpressing
C4A
in mice reduced cortical synapse density, increased microglial engulfment of synapses and altered mouse behavior.

results.finding: In 14 mice, optogenetic activation of parvalbumin neurons improved cognition after anti-NMDAR antibody exposure (n=7 per group; P<0.05).
results.detail: Patient-derived antibodies induced cognitive impairment; activation improved Y-maze and novel object recognition performance. This tests an autoimmune encephalitis mechanism, not a partition of primary psychiatric syndromes.
results.quote: After 7 days of antibody injection, ChR2-expressing mice performed better cognitively than control mice in the Y-maze and NOR tests

results.finding: EDIT-B bipolar disorder test in 393 patients: sensitivity 82.6%.
results.detail: Specificity was 80.3% against major depressive disorder. Results are relative to physician diagnoses in patients experiencing a major depressive episode; they do not establish causal disease identity. The test combines RNA biomarkers with clinical and treatment data.
results.quote: In 393 patients with current major depressive episode (238 MDD; 155 BD), EDIT-B demonstrated robust performance: area under the curve-receiver operating characteristic of 0.873 (95% CI 0.837 to 0.909), sensitivity of 82.6% (95% CI 75.7% to 88.2%) and specificity of 80.3% (95% CI 74.6% to 85.1%).

results.finding: PGx-guided antidepressant treatment: 629 patients across three trials; pooled functional disability difference was −2.85 points.
results.detail: The three trials had mixed functional results. The pooled effect was not significant with the Hartung–Knapp adjustment, heterogeneity was substantial, and overall evidence certainty was very low. Reproducible functional improvement was not established.
results.quote:
Three studies were included in random-effect meta-analyses. In these, PGx-guided antidepressant
treatment significantly decreased functional disability, measured by the Sheehan Disability Scale/Inventory
(SDS/I),comparedtoTAU(k=3,MeanDifference=-2.85, SE=1.32[95%CI:-5.44,-0.26], p=.031).
